new_behaviours.behaviour: NB-1: HostedEnvironment applies `.modifier(AppZoomModifier(percent: model.settings.appZoom))` to every hosted view tree: each window root through HostedRoot at :150, and each separately hosted chat column at RootView.swift:280. It sits after the model and liveResize environment and before `.buttonBorderShape(.capsule)` and ThemeTint. The sidebar, Settings and composer therefore scale together. No requirement in porting/spec/*.json or ui_contract.json mentions app zoom: `grep -rli 'appZoom|AppZoom|app zoom'` returned no files.

This is a supporting file in another batch, reached only through the NB-1 call site. AppZoomModifier (:18-27) normalizes the percent and computes scale = percent/100. It wraps content.scaleEffect(scale, anchor: .topLeading) in ZoomLayout (:31-51). ZoomLayout proposes the unscaled viewport (proposal / scale), reports the fitted size multiplied by scale, and places the content at bounds.origin with a topLeading anchor, so the content reflows instead of clipping. AppZoom.levels = [75, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200] (:6). normalized() maps any value outside the list to 100 (:8-10). next(_:increasing:) steps to the adjacent level and holds at either end (:12-15). The file does not exist at dd2b86ef.

Supporting setting referenced by the NB-1 call site; it belongs to another batch. appZoom: Int is stored under the UserDefaults key "appZoom" (:131), saved in didSet (:253-254), and loaded as AppZoom.normalized(defaults.object(forKey: "appZoom") as? Int ?? 100) (:718). The default is 100. It is absent at dd2b86ef.

new_behaviours.behaviour: New shared ISO 8601 helper enum. No requirement covers it. It holds two public Date.ISO8601FormatStyle values: `fractional` (includingFractionalSeconds: true, :10) and `plain` (default, :13).

ISO8601.date(from:) tries the fractional-seconds style first, then the whole-second style, and returns nil for anything else. At 1fbf81e it is used by UpdateChecker.swift:325, AntigravitySession.swift:577 and :594, CodexSession.swift:472, CopilotSession.swift:471, PlanLimits.swift:334 and TokenLedger.swift:585. The caller files belong to other batches. Possible caller drift: at dd2b86 AntigravitySession.swift:574 and :591 and PlanLimits.swift:334 used a bare ISO8601DateFormatter() with no fractional option, so a stamp with fractional seconds that returned nil there may now parse. Whether the old bare formatter rejected fractional stamps was not tested (UNKNOWN). UpdateChecker, CodexSession and TokenLedger already built both a fractional and a plain formatter at dd2b86 (`git grep` at dd2b86: UpdateChecker.swift:325,328; CodexSession.swift:469,471; TokenLedger.swift:589,592).

ISO8601.dateOnly(from:) parses a bare date `2026-09-13` via a private year().month().day() style. The doc comment says it is for GitHub Copilot's quota endpoint. It is used by CopilotSession.swift:471 as `ISO8601.date(from: text) ?? ISO8601.dateOnly(from: text)`. At dd2b86 CopilotSession.swift:470-475 used ISO8601DateFormatter() and then formatOptions = [.withFullDate].

ISO8601.string(from:) formats with the plain style: whole seconds, UTC, `Z` suffix (doc :28, shape per :12). It is used by HangWatchdog.swift:88 for the hang report file stamp, and by OpenAICompatibleSession.swift:1212 for the "Today's date is ..." prompt line, which at dd2b86 used ISO8601DateFormatter().string(from: Date()).

New `String.trimmed` computed property, equal to `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)`. The doc comment says narrower sets keep trimmingCharacters(in:). It is a helper with identical semantics and no new observable behaviour. `git grep` at 1fbf81e found `.trimmed` in 55 Swift files. Across all Swift files, the count of lines containing `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` fell from 175 at dd2b86 to 21 at 1fbf81e.

New doc comment on OnceContinuation: the continuation is taken out under the lock and resumed outside it, because a resume runs whatever the awaiting task does next and `withLock` is non-reentrant. This documents a discipline that already existed at dd2b86, so it adds no runtime behaviour. A port using a non-reentrant lock should keep the resume outside the lock.

files.summary: New 138-line @MainActor enum TerminalFont. preferred(fallbackSize: 12) reads the configured fonts of Ghostty (config file font-family/font-size), iTerm2 (New Bookmarks 'Normal Font') and Terminal.app (the default profile's archived Font), with running terminals first. It returns the first one that covers the Nerd Font probe glyphs U+E0B0, U+E0B6, U+F015 and U+F0035. Failing that, it tries the Nerd sibling family of the first configured font, then the first installed family containing 'nerd font', then the configured font itself, and last the 12pt regular monospaced system font. Font names are normalised: lowercased, spaces and hyphens removed, 'nerdfont' shortened to 'nf'. No requirement covers this file.

new_behaviours.behaviour: The embedded terminal font is TerminalFont.preferred(), evaluated once per TerminalSession init (new tab, script tab, restart). It is no longer a fixed 12pt monospaced system font.

The preferred(fallbackSize: 12) selection chain: (1) the first configured terminal font that covers all Nerd probe glyphs; (2) if any font is configured, the Nerd sibling family of the first configured font at its point size; (3) else the first installed Nerd Font at that size; (4) else the first configured font itself. With no configured font: the first installed Nerd Font at 12pt, else NSFont.monospacedSystemFont(ofSize: 12, weight: .regular).

Configured fonts are read from three terminals, in the order Ghostty (com.mitchellh.ghostty), iTerm2 (com.googlecode.iterm2), Terminal.app (com.apple.Terminal). Terminals currently running (NSWorkspace.runningApplications bundle IDs) are moved ahead of the rest, and the original order is kept within each group.

Ghostty config parsing. Lines are trimmed. Lines starting with '#' or lacking '=' are skipped. The key and value are split on the first '='. The first 'font-family' wins: the first comma-separated name, with spaces and double quotes trimmed. 'font-size' is taken only if it parses as a Double > 0; the last such value wins; the default is 12. The first config file that yields a resolvable font is used.
Ghostty config locations, in order: ~/Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config, then ~/.config/ghostty/config.

Terminal.app font. From the com.apple.Terminal defaults, the profile named by 'Default Window Settings' (fallback 'Basic') is looked up in 'Window Settings'. Its 'Font' Data is unarchived as an NSFont with NSKeyedUnarchiver.

iTerm2 font. The first profile in the com.googlecode.iterm2 'New Bookmarks' array whose 'Normal Font' string ends in a numeric size (format '<PostScriptName> <size>') and resolves through NSFont(name:size:).
Nerd Font detection: the font's coveredCharacterSet must contain all four probes U+E0B0 (powerline cap), U+E0B6, U+F015 and U+F0035 (a supplementary-plane Material icon).

nerdSibling looks for an installed family whose normalized name equals normalized(familyName) + 'nf', at the same point size (e.g. 'Geist Mono' -> 'GeistMono Nerd Font'). firstInstalledNerdFont takes the first family in NSFontManager.availableFontFamilies whose name contains 'nerd font', case-insensitively.

Tolerant font-name resolution: exact NSFont(name:size:) first, then a family whose normalized name matches. normalized() lowercases, removes spaces and hyphens, and replaces 'nerdfont' with 'nf', so 'Geist Mono NF' resolves to 'GeistMono Nerd Font'.

The terminal tab's restart and close glyphs now use Chrome.secondaryText, which at 1fbf81e is labelColor at 0.7 per Chrome.swift:79 (out of batch). They previously used the hierarchical .secondary foreground style. Recorded as CHANGED on PR-TERM-022/023 and UI-TERM-006/007.

The live-resize observer closures run their bodies inside MainActor.assumeIsolated. This is a Swift 6 isolation assertion; the observers are still on queue: .main, so observable behaviour is unchanged. Listed for completeness only.

Fixed .system(size:) fonts are replaced by system text styles: .body, .callout, .subheadline, .footnote and .title3. Whether these now scale with any macOS text-size or accessibility setting, and so render differently from the old fixed sizes on a non-default configuration, is UNKNOWN; it was not verified on macOS. Recorded as CHANGED on the affected requirements and UI records.

new_behaviours.behaviour: HydraRightTapHost's deinit now runs `MainActor.assumeIsolated { removeMonitor() }`. assumeIsolated is a runtime check that traps if deinit runs off the main actor; before, removeMonitor() was called directly. The visible behaviour is the same: the monitor is still removed on deinit. No requirement covers this isolation check. Only relevant if the port frees this host off the UI thread.

new_behaviours.file: DroppyCode/UI/Common/AppZoom.swift (outside batch D03; replaces the chat zoom removed from ChatView.swift:120-123)
new_behaviours.behaviour: A new app-wide zoom scales every window root and chat column with scaleEffect plus a reflowing Layout. Levels are 75, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175 and 200; any other stored value normalizes to 100. The setting is the UserDefaults key "appZoom" (AppSettings.swift:131,253,718). The menu gains Zoom In, Zoom Out and Actual Size (AppCommands.swift:53-60). grep for appZoom/AppZoom over porting/spec/*.json and porting/ui_contract.json found no match, so no requirement covers it. Listed here for routing only: it belongs to the batch that owns these files.

new_behaviours.behaviour: Per-provider expansion state @State providerExpansion: [ProviderKind: Bool], held on the page so search rebuilds do not reset it. A missing entry means expanded (get: providerExpansion[provider] ?? true). It is not persisted to settings: no AppSettings key was added in this file.

The provider section header is a toggle button in ChromeQuietButtonStyle (no pressed feedback) that toggles isExpanded inside withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide). It adds a trailing chevron.right at .system(size: 11, weight: .semibold) in Chrome.secondaryText, rotated 90 degrees when expanded. Tooltip: "Hide the model list" or "Show the model list". accessibilityLabel is the provider name. accessibilityValue is "Expanded" or "Collapsed". accessibilityHint is "Shows or hides the model list". It has the .isHeader trait.

Row visibility rules. With a search, only matching models are visible. Without a search, an expanded section shows all catalogue models and a collapsed section shows only models already in the picker, always in catalogue order. A collapsed section with no chosen models hides its card entirely (cardVisible = isExpanded || isFiltering || !visibleIDs.isEmpty).

The card is an eager VStack replacing ChromeCard (same Chrome.overlay(0.03) fill and cardCornerRadius, plus a clipShape). Every catalogue row and its divider sit in a ChromeRevealLayout (height reveal, fraction 0 or 1, animatable). A divider shows only above a visible row that is not the first visible row. Hidden rows and a hidden card are .disabled, .allowsHitTesting(false) and .accessibilityHidden. .animation(nil, value: query) keeps search re-filtering instant while header toggles animate.
Adding or removing a catalogue model is unanimated while a search is active, and animated with Chrome.panelSlide otherwise.
The 'Loading models…'/'No models loaded' row with 'Load models' appears only for an empty unfiltered catalogue, and collapses with the section when it is collapsed and not filtering.

The custom server editor has a responsive height: min(560, (kind == .stdio ? 450 : 320) + variables.count * 34), with width 380 (Self.width), sectionSpacing 12, outerPadding 16 and variableRowHeight 34. Switching kind or adding or removing a variable row resizes the popover.

The editor footer is a VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10) below the ScrollView holding the error line (.subheadline, Chrome.danger, 3 lines) and the save row (Spacer(minLength: 0), then 'Add server'/'Save' in .glassProminent). It never scrolls out of reach.
The custom editor close button has a 24x24 frame, a rect content shape and a new accessibility label "Close".
The custom editor Name field is now styled like the Hydra pair editor's name field: plain style, focus effect disabled, .title3 semibold in Chrome.primaryText, padding 10/7, on mcpFieldSurface.

New private View.mcpFieldSurface(): background(Chrome.overlay(0.06), in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 9, style: .continuous)). It is applied to the name, command, URL, key and value fields (horizontal padding now 10) and to the arguments TextEditor (padding 6/4, commented as matching the single-line text edge).
The 'Read the docs' arrow glyph is .system(.caption2, weight: .bold): 10pt nominal, was 9.
The release section popover draws the version line, bullets and rollup all in Chrome.secondaryText. Previously they were .tertiary, .secondary and .tertiary.

Inline markdown is stripped with Swift Regex literals and String.replacing instead of static NSRegularExpression objects. The comment now says per-bullet cost is acceptable because parse memoizes on the raw notes. The patterns and order are the same, so there is no user-visible behaviour change unless the grapheme and UTF-16 matching difference matters (UNKNOWN, not tested).

Four buttons are added to the CommandGroup(after: .sidebar) View group after the existing divider: 'Zoom In' (Cmd-+), 'Zoom Out' (Cmd--) and 'Actual Size' (Cmd-0, sets appZoom = 100), plus a hidden second 'Zoom In' on Cmd-= for US keyboards (:53-62). They step settings.appZoom through AppZoom.next over [75, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200] (UI/Common/AppZoom.swift:6-15). The chords are hard-coded, not taken from ShortcutStore. Every later line moves down by 10.

HydraTreeCache is rewritten (:21-107). Captures now use git.currentTree(), which is incremental, instead of captureTree(). They are tagged with a generation that invalidate() bumps, and a fresh capture is reused only while currentTree still matches it. A capture or in-flight task from an older generation is discarded, and a failed or cancelled task clears its inFlight entry. hydraUnmergedFileCount drops the lastMergedTurnStart shortcut (:283-293). startDroppyHead stamps executionStartedAt and clears executionFinishedAt before sending the brief (:519-527). hydraHeadTurnFinished stamps executionFinishedAt (:636-638). waitForSettledCheckout now reads leadRuntime.hydraCurrentTurnTouchedPaths instead of hydraChatContext().touchedPaths (:818-825). applyHydraHead stamps landingStartedAt/landingFinishedAt (:839-844), and its operation-in-progress error text becomes 'a rebase or merge is underway in the checkout, or its git state cannot be read' (:851). The remaining edits are trimmingCharacters -> .trimmed (identical, Core/Support/Text.swift:132).

Largest change. The resume sweep sorts leads by UUID string, loads every runtime first, and gates on isReadyForHydraMerge. It no longer needs a completed unmerged turn, and it counts a head only when its landing 'landed' (:41-72). autoMergeHydraWork adds guards !isAnyHydraMergeRunning and isReadyForHydraMerge, then re-checks readiness after the landing wait (:76-104). Groups are always built, and a new cross-group held check records a hold and stops the job (:125-147). The post-merge leftover note is deleted, and settlement records/notes are added (:152-182, :829-833). mergeHydraProject re-checks readiness and current sibling claims after captureTree(paths:) (:247-259). glab mr create gains --squash-before-merge (:382). hydraWork drops the timestamp shortcut, excludes heads whose landing is a patch or errored, subtracts only blocking claims, filters turnIDs/headIDs by claimed files and returns a held map (:471-613). siblingOwnedPaths returns reserved/blocking maps with owner titles and a UUID ordering between finished jobs (:634-676). New helpers: hydraIsFinishedIdleEligible, hydraHasPendingLanding, hydraRanksAfter, canStillMerge, recordHydraSettlement, recordHydraHold, heldDetail (:679-851). The remaining edits are trim spelling only.

One line: rename(_:to:) at :749 now uses 'title.trimmed' instead of 'title.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)'. String.trimmed is defined as exactly that call (Core/Support/Text.swift:132 at 1fbf81e), so behaviour is identical. No line shift.

New setting chronologicalTimeline: key 'chronologicalTimeline', Bool, default false (:128, :234-239, :715). The chatZoom setting is replaced by appZoom: key 'chatZoom' becomes 'appZoom', and an Int index into ChatZoom (default ChatZoom.defaultIndex, clamped) becomes an Int percent normalized to AppZoom.levels (default 100). It is now an app-wide window scale (:131, :251-255, :718). The old key is no longer read. Lines after 127 shift by 1, and lines after 232 shift by 8 to 9.

Downloader synchronisation only: the NSLock guarding two stored vars becomes 'Mutex(State())' (import Synchronization at :4), holding continuation and destination (:456-466, :479, :483, :489-491, :506). Download behaviour, timeouts, messages and progress are unchanged. Lines after 3 shift by 1, and lines after 454 by 7.

AppVersion init and text(ofTag:) change trimmingCharacters to .trimmed, which is identical (:11, :30). GitLabRelease.parseDate becomes a delegate 'ISO8601.date(from: text)' (:324-326). The parse lives in Core/Support/ISO8601.swift:19-21: Date.ISO8601FormatStyle with fractional seconds, then without, in the same order as the two former ISO8601DateFormatter instances. Byte-identical acceptance for inputs outside the two documented shapes was not tested: UNKNOWN. Not marked cosmetic only for that reason. Lines after 330 shift by -5.

requirements.detail: Same candidate filter and same 259200 s window: old HydraMerge:38 'Date.now.addingTimeInterval(-3 * 24 * 3600)' is now HydraMerge:50 'Date.now.addingTimeInterval(-Self.hydraMergeWindow)' with hydraMergeWindow = 3 * 24 * 3600 at :41. The filter is unchanged at :51. The new uuid sort (:52) is recorded under PR-HYDRAMERGE-006.

Old (:41-43), per lead in list order: 'let runtime = self.runtime(for: lead.id); await runtime.ensureLoaded(); guard runtime.phase == .idle, !runtime.isHydraMerging, runningHydraHeads(of: lead.id) == 0 else { continue }'. New (:52-60): candidates are sorted by id.uuidString ascending. A first loop loads every candidate runtime before any merge. A second loop takes existingRuntime(for:) and requires 'runtime.isReadyForHydraMerge, !runtime.isHydraMerging'. isReadyForHydraMerge (ThreadRuntime.swift:2485-2490) = phase == .idle && !isLoadingHistory && !isReverting && pendingSend == nil && turns.last?.status == .completed && !hasWorkingHeads && hydraPendingReports.isEmpty && hydraBatches.isEmpty && hydraWaiting.isEmpty && !hydraFlushScheduled. runningHydraHeads is no longer consulted here.

Old (:44-45): 'guard !finished.isEmpty, runtime.turns.last?.status == .completed else { continue }'. That guard is deleted at 1fbf81e, so at least one completed unmerged turn is no longer required. The comment at :62-65 explains why: a lead whose turns are all booked spent, but whose head landing never went out, must still merge. The last-turn-completed test survives only inside isReadyForHydraMerge (ThreadRuntime.swift:2487). 'finished' is still computed at :66.

The head criterion changed. Old (:50): '$0.mergedAt == nil && !($0.landing?.files ?? []).isEmpty'. New (:70): '$0.mergedAt == nil && ($0.landing?.landed ?? false)', where landed = !files.isEmpty && patchPath == nil && error == nil (Core/Models/Hydra.swift:475). A head whose landing was kept as a patch or errored no longer counts as own work. The turn criterion is unchanged (:69).

The old guard (:59-60) had six conditions ending '!runtime.isHydraMerging else { return }'. The new guard (:85-87) adds '!isAnyHydraMergeRunning', so there is one merge app-wide and a skipped job is left to the resume sweep (comment :79-84). It also adds 'runtime.isReadyForHydraMerge'. That makes eight preconditions, not six.

The await on runtime.hydraLanding is unchanged (old :73-76 -> new :100-103). A new check follows it at :104: 'guard runtime.isReadyForHydraMerge else { return }', a silent exit. It is listed as new behaviour.

Old (:87): 'groups = own.paths.isEmpty ? [] : [(project, ownCheckout, own)]'. New (:125): the own group is always added. Empty-path groups are removed later at :147 'groups.removeAll { $0.work.paths.isEmpty }', after the new held check (:135-146) has looked at every group.

Old (:96-99): 'if !work.paths.isEmpty { groups.append(...) }'. New (:124-125): the group is appended unconditionally and pruned at :147 after the held check. The failure case's pointer to the leftover-count report is stale: that report is removed (PR-HYDRAMERGE-027), and the comment at :111 now says such work 'stays behind without a word'.

The marking-spent path is kept (:152-155). It now runs only after the held check found nothing (:135-146), and it is no longer always silent. New :156-158: 'if runtime.hydraMerges.last?.outcome == .held { recordHydraSettlement(...) }'. When hydraUnmergedFileCount == 0, that appends a record with outcome .settled and posts the note 'Hydra has no files left to merge.' / 'The checkout has no remaining changes from this job to send. No new merge request was needed.' (:829-833).
The stray-only record and note are unchanged (old :118-120 -> new :161-163). This path is now reached only after the new held check (:135-146) found no claim and after empty groups are pruned (:147).

Sequential merge and abort-before-marking are unchanged (old :123-127 -> :166-170; enum :21-25 same). mergeHydraProject has new .failed exits (:249-259, see PR-HYDRAMERGE-033). A run where every group is .alreadyOnMain and there are no strays now also calls recordHydraSettlement (:180-182).
The marking code is unchanged (old :128-132 -> :171-175). The turnIDs/headIDs it marks are now filtered in hydraWork (see PR-HYDRAMERGE-078).

The stray record and note are unchanged (old :133-136 -> :176-179). The hunk at old :137 removes the leftover loop (PR-HYDRAMERGE-027) and adds a new else-branch at :180-182: when every group is .alreadyOnMain, recordHydraSettlement runs.

The post-merge leftover inspection at old :138-150 is deleted at 1fbf81e. It took a fresh captureTree per group, compared changedPaths against HEAD, and subtracted build output, ignored paths and sibling paths. It posted the note 'Hydra merged <project>, but left a changed file no turn or head recorded.' / '... Still uncommitted in that checkout: name them in a brief, or commit them there by hand.'. It is replaced by '} else if outcomes.allSatisfy({ $0 == .alreadyOnMain }) { recordHydraSettlement(...) }' (:180-182).

New steps sit between captureTree(paths:) and the HEAD-tree comparison (:247-259). First 'guard runtime.isReadyForHydraMerge else { return .failed }', which writes no record and no note. Then 'let currentClaims = siblingOwnedPaths(...).blocking'. If another chat currently holds any team path, recordHydraHold(held, ...) runs and the pass returns .failed. Only then does the unchanged .alreadyOnMain comparison run (:263).
Only the trim spelling changed: old :622 trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) -> new :770 '.trimmed'. The two are identical (Core/Support/Text.swift:132). Lines 617-622 -> 765-770.
Only the trim spelling of the lead reply changed (old :642 -> :790, identical per Text.swift:132). The body strings are unchanged. Lines 626-650 -> 774-798.

Old argv (:337): ['mr','create','--title',title,'--description',body,'--yes']. New argv (:382): ['mr','create','--title',title,'--description',body,'--yes','--squash-before-merge']. So squash is no longer 'left to the project's defaults and never passed'. The doc comment now reads 'Squash and source-branch removal are explicit for GitLab team merges.' (:373). --repo and --source-branch/--target-branch are unchanged (:383-391).
Credential stripping is unchanged (old :338-345 -> :383-390). The overlap is only the argv line above it (see PR-HYDRAMERGE-048).

The heads section format is unchanged (old :283-293 -> :328-338). Which heads reach work.heads changed in hydraWork (see PR-HYDRAMERGE-068).

The comment at old :294-297 (-> :339-342) and the success-note content are unchanged. The expected result is stale, though. It says 'Only the stray note (PR-HYDRAMERGE-026) and the unrecorded-leftover note (PR-HYDRAMERGE-027) report anything held back'. The leftover note is removed. A new hold note exists: 'Hydra is waiting for another chat's files.' (:840). So does a new settlement note: 'Hydra has no files left to merge.' (:832).

Old (:429-438): 'lastMergedTurnStart = runtime.turns.last { $0.hydraMerged }?.startedAt', and a head is skipped when 'finished < lastMergedTurnStart'. New (:481-484): 'guard let info = head.hydra, info.mergedAt == nil, info.landing?.patchPath == nil, info.landing?.error == nil else { continue }'. The timestamp shortcut is removed (comment :474-479), and a head whose landing is a patch or errored is now excluded. headIDs are derived at :609 (see PR-HYDRAMERGE-078).
Only the trim spelling changed (old :449 -> :493, identical). Lines 440-456 -> 484-500.
Name, index and task are unchanged (old :481 -> :525). The tuple only gains head.id as its first element.
Only the trim spelling changed (old :491 -> :535, identical). Lines 484-499 -> 528-543.

Old siblingOwnedPaths (:549-567) returned a Set<String>, and hydraWork did 'paths.subtract(siblingPaths)' (:529). New siblingOwnedPaths (:634-676) returns '(reserved: [String: String], blocking: [String: String])', mapping each path to the owning chat's title. A sibling head with no mergedAt reserves only when 'info.status == .running || parent.map(canStillMerge) == true' (:654). A non-head chat's unmerged turns reserve only 'where canStillMerge(other) || turn.status != .completed' (:671). A claim does not block when its lead is a finished, idle, eligible job that ranks after this one by UUID string (:659-660, :670, :699-701). hydraWork subtracts only blocking claims (:586-587). Claimed files now hold the whole job (recordHydraHold) instead of being silently left out.

The sweep shape is unchanged (old :516-524 -> :568-576), but the filter changed. Old: 'fresh.filter { !siblingPaths.contains($0) }'. New: 'fresh.filter { !siblingClaims.contains($0) }', with siblingClaims = Set(siblingFiles.reserved.keys) (:566), the new reservation set of PR-HYDRAMERGE-075.

new_behaviours.behaviour: The View group (after .sidebar) gains, after its divider: 'Zoom In' on Cmd-+ (AppZoom.next increasing), 'Zoom Out' on Cmd-- (decreasing), 'Actual Size' on Cmd-0 (appZoom = 100), and a hidden 'Zoom In' on Cmd-= for US keyboards. The chords are hard-coded rather than taken from ShortcutStore. No UI record or requirement covers these items.

AppZoom.levels = [75, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200]. normalized() maps anything else to 100. next() steps to the neighbouring level and stays put at either end. AppZoomModifier scales the whole window, with a layout that proposes the unscaled viewport. The consumers WindowManager.swift:175 and SettingsView.swift:455 (AppZoomCard) belong to other batches.

New setting chronologicalTimeline: key 'chronologicalTimeline', Bool, default false, persisted in didSet. It shows the running turn's rows in arrival order instead of folding earlier steps into the working line. Consumers are ThreadTimeline.swift:1861 and TimelineRows.swift:2492 (other batches).
New setting appZoom: key 'appZoom', Int percent, default 100, normalized to AppZoom.levels on read, persisted in didSet. It replaces chatZoom. The old 'chatZoom' key is neither read nor migrated.

HydraTreeCache generations. Each capture records the generation it began in, and invalidate() bumps the checkout's generation. A stored capture is reused only if its generation is current, it is under 3 s old, and git.currentTree() still equals its tree. An in-flight task is joined only if it began in the current generation. A result from an older generation is discarded and the capture is redone. A failed or cancelled task clears inFlight. Task.checkCancellation runs between awaits. The tree comes from git.currentTree(), the incremental watch snapshot (Git.swift:433, another batch).
Just before a Droppy-run head's brief is sent, HydraHeadInfo.executionStartedAt = now and executionFinishedAt = nil are persisted, so a head steered on is timed on the new turn.
When a Droppy-run head's turn ends, HydraHeadInfo.executionFinishedAt = now is persisted, whatever the outcome.

applyHydraHead persists landingStartedAt = now and landingFinishedAt = nil once the head, lead and checkout guards pass, and a defer sets landingFinishedAt = now on every exit. A landing that never got that far keeps neither stamp. These feed HydraRunMetricsView.swift:177-184 (another batch).
New landing error text for an operation in progress: 'a rebase or merge is underway in the checkout, or its git state cannot be read'.

waitForSettledCheckout decides whether the lead is busy on the patch's paths using leadRuntime.hydraCurrentTurnTouchedPaths, a runtime set of checkout-relative paths (ThreadRuntime.swift:505). It no longer walks the timeline through hydraChatContext.
hydraMergeWindow = 3 * 24 * 3600 s is shared by the resume sweep cutoff and canStillMerge. A head's claim on its files lapses once its lead has been quiet for longer than this window.
The resume sweep sorts candidate leads by id.uuidString, loads every runtime before choosing, and gates each on runtime.isReadyForHydraMerge (ThreadRuntime.swift:2485-2490) && !isHydraMerging.

autoMergeHydraWork refuses to start while any merge is running app-wide (!isAnyHydraMergeRunning) or while the lead is not isReadyForHydraMerge; the skipped job is picked up by the resume sweep. After awaiting an in-flight landing, it re-checks readiness and returns silently if the lead is no longer ready.

Cross-group hold. Every group's held map is joined into absolute paths (checkout + relative path). If any file is held by another chat, recordHydraHold runs and the job returns: nothing is merged, marked or spent. Only after that are groups with no paths removed.

recordHydraSettlement runs when a job that last recorded a hold turns out to have nothing to send. It also runs when every group came back .alreadyOnMain and there were no strays. It acts only when hydraUnmergedFileCount == 0, then appends HydraMergeRecord(outcome: .settled, files: 0, detail: nil) and posts the note title 'Hydra has no files left to merge.' with body 'The checkout has no remaining changes from this job to send. No new merge request was needed.'

recordHydraHold. When the last record is already .held with the same detail, it does nothing. Otherwise it appends HydraMergeRecord(outcome: .held, files: held.count, detail) and posts the note title 'Hydra is waiting for another chat's files.' with body detail + ' The work stays in the checkout. Hydra retries after the other chat finishes or its queued merge completes.' The detail is built by heldDetail: '1 file the team changed is' or '<N> files the team changed are', then ' also claimed by <sorted unique chat titles joined ", ">: <up to 6 backticked sorted paths joined ", ">[ and <N-6> more].'

In mergeHydraProject, after captureTree(paths:), the lead's readiness is checked again: if it is not ready, the pass returns .failed silently. Then the current blocking sibling claims are recomputed; if any team path is held, recordHydraHold runs and the pass returns .failed, so newly active shared work is not pushed.
glab mr create now passes '--squash-before-merge' after '--yes'.

hydraWork skips heads whose landing has a patchPath or an error, and removes only blocking claims ('claimed'). It books as merged only the turns and heads with no claimed file, and returns held = claimed path -> holding chat title as a new sixth tuple element (typealias at :32).

siblingOwnedPaths returns (reserved, blocking), each path mapped to the owner chat's title (the parent's title for a head). A running sibling head always reserves its files. A finished head reserves only while its lead can still merge (canStillMerge). A non-head chat's completed unmerged turns reserve only while canStillMerge; its incomplete turns always reserve. A claim does not block when it belongs to a completed head, or a chat, whose lead is finished, idle and eligible and ranks after this job by UUID string.

New predicates. hydraIsFinishedIdleEligible: Hydra on, live runtime, isReadyForHydraMerge, not merging, no pending landing, and canStillMerge. hydraHasPendingLanding: a team head with no mergedAt whose landing has files but did not land. hydraRanksAfter: lead.id.uuidString > other.uuidString. canStillMerge: true when the live runtime is not idle or is merging. Otherwise it requires the lead to be unarchived, have Hydra on, and have been updated within hydraMergeWindow. Without a live runtime, lastStatus must also be .completed. With one, the last turn must be completed and there must be either unmerged turns or landed, unmerged head work.
HydraMergeRecord.Outcome gains 'held' and 'settled' (raw values 'held', 'settled'), which the new hold and settlement paths persist in the thread document.
The GitLab merge of a Hydra request runs 'glab mr merge <n> --yes --squash --remove-source-branch' (was '--yes' only). This was seen in the diff only; it is outside batch D01.

batch: D02 (DroppyCode/App/Runtime): upstream drift dd2b86ef (v1.6.0) to 1fbf81e (v1.6.2). Method: I ran `git -C E:/Droppy/reference/droppy-code-417ab7d3 diff dd2b86ef..1fbf81e -- DroppyCode/App/Runtime/ThreadRuntime.swift`. The stat line was "1 file changed, 176 insertions(+), 55 deletions(-)". I read the whole diff and the full old and new files, plus the helper types at 1fbf81e: HydraDelegationBudget (Hydra.swift:559-617), interruptedBlockMessage and droppedBlockNotice (Hydra.swift:1075-1088), ProviderKind.supportsCompact (Provider.swift:149-154), HydraDelegationStreamParser (HydraDelegationStream.swift:129-226, which already existed at the pinned commit), and ProviderEvent `case tokenSpend` (ProviderSession.swift:104). A Python scan of porting/spec/*.json and porting/ui_contract.json found every record citing ThreadRuntime.swift: 283 requirements and 36 UI records. The 36 UI records are the same IDs in spec `ui` arrays and in ui_contract.json. I compared every cited old line range with its shifted new range, line by line. 278 records have identical text, and all 19 that differ were reviewed by hand. Records that describe a behaviour touched by the new code were also reviewed by hand, even where their cited lines are unchanged. Result: 21 CHANGED, 1 MOVED, 297 UNAFFECTED, 0 REMOVED. No Swift compiler was run. The claim that the second `.tokenSpend` arm is unreachable comes from reading the source and is UNVERIFIED. Nothing was modified.

files.summary: Behaviour changes: (1) /compact is now gated on ProviderKind.supportsCompact, which adds Claude. (2) The ACPSession arm adds .opencodeGo. (3) New .tokenSpend handling: two arms in handle(), recordTokenSpend, pendingNativeSpend, and hydraTokens recomputed on install for Droppy heads. (4) The delegation counters move into HydraDelegationBudget, with a new drop notice put in front of the lead's next prompt when a block is dropped (refusal cap, or turn stopped or failed before heads went out). (5) The streamed delegation scan now uses the incremental HydraDelegationStreamParser (delegationParser, endDelegationStream), and the round cap gates only the first read of a block. (6) New hydraCurrentTurnTouchedPaths is kept up to date as edits land and is read by AppModel+Hydra. (7) Revert now clears hydraTouched. (8) Droppy-head startTurn resets startedAt, queuedAt and executionStartedAt and clears executionFinishedAt, landingStartedAt and landingFinishedAt. (9) hydraWaiting entries carry queuedAt, which is written onto the spawned head. (10) New public isReadyForHydraMerge. Not cosmetic.

handle(_:) (new :2119-2250) now switches over 31 ProviderEvent cases, because ProviderSession.swift:104 at 1fbf81e adds `case tokenSpend(TokenSpend)`. It still has no default arm. new_behaviours.behaviour: New ProviderEvent .tokenSpend arm (the first of two). While a turn is current, it appends the TokenSpend to that turn's tokenSpends and does saveRevision += 1, with no scheduleSave and no merge. This is the arm that actually runs, including for spends rehearsed onto a head through .agentEvent.

Second .tokenSpend arm plus supporting code. For a spend with an agentID on a thread that is not a native head, it forwards the spend to that native head's runtime.recordTokenSpend, or buffers it in pendingNativeSpend[agentID] until hydraAgentStarted flushes it to the new head. Otherwise it calls recordTokenSpend. recordTokenSpend ignores totalTokens <= 0. It targets the current turn, or the last turn on a native head, merges into an existing spend with the same provider, model and agentID (TokenSpend.merge), adds to hydraTokens on a Droppy head, bumps saveRevision and calls scheduleSave. Because an earlier arm matches .tokenSpend first, this arm appears unreachable. That is from reading the source only; nothing was compiled, so it is UNVERIFIED.
install(_:) on a Droppy-run head sets hydraTokens to the sum of TokenSpend.totalTokens across all loaded turns' tokenSpends.

At the end of install(_:): with no current turn, it resets the delegation stream and parser and clears hydraCurrentTurnTouchedPaths. With a turn in flight, it re-records the edits of every tool entry of that turn into hydraCurrentTurnTouchedPaths (native head events can arrive while history loads).

New public read-only set hydraCurrentTurnTouchedPaths: the checkout-relative paths the current turn has touched so far. It is fed by recordCurrentTurnEdits, which runs only while a turn is current and uses TouchedPaths.relative against workingRoot. It is fed from upsertTool (before capping), applyToolUpdate, settleCommand (current-turn rows), noteHydraEdits, native-head command settles and rehearseTurn(touchedPaths:). It is cleared in startTurn, in revert and in install when idle. finishTurn adds the finished set to it and does not clear it, so it keeps the last turn's paths. It is consumed at AppModel+Hydra.swift:825 (`!wanted.isDisjoint(with: leadRuntime.hydraCurrentTurnTouchedPaths)`), which is outside this batch.
revert now clears hydraTouched (pending native-head paths) and hydraCurrentTurnTouchedPaths after removing the turns.

At every startTurn of a Droppy-run head (thread.hydra.kind == .droppy), the head record is updated. When turns.count > 1: startedAt = .now, queuedAt = nil, executionStartedAt = .now. Always: executionFinishedAt, landingStartedAt and landingFinishedAt are set to nil. The new HydraHeadInfo fields are read by HydraRunMetricsView.swift:177-180 (outside this batch).

Each waiting delegated task records queuedAt = Date.now when it is queued (in the streamed top-up, the normal block path and the streamed scan). When spawnWaitingHeads spawns it, the head record gets queuedAt = that queue time.

Just before session.send, a pending dropped-block notice (hydraBudget.takeDropNotice()) is put in front of the whole prompt, outside the continuation, anti-slop, delegation request and Hydra prefixes. It is used once. It is taken only once the send is about to run, so a turn that aborts while starting keeps it waiting. The notice text is "[Hydra] " + message + "

---

" (Hydra.swift:1086-1088). It is applied to any next turn, including a user's own message and, from reading the code, a slash-command message, since there is no slash-command guard.

When a stopped or failed turn drops an unsent delegation block (dropDelegationBlock, second branch), the lead is now also told on its next turn: hydraBudget.noteDropped(HydraPrompts.interruptedBlockMessage(stopped:)). The verbatim text (Hydra.swift:1075-1081) is "No heads went out.\nYour reply's delegation block was dropped: the turn was stopped|failed before the heads could go out, and none of that work was delegated. Do it yourself, or send the block again."

Past maxRefusals (3), refuseBlock still writes the 'No heads went out' timeline note and ends the turn as a plain reply. HydraDelegationBudget.refuse now also queues the refusal message as a drop notice for the lead's next turn.

The streamed delegation read now keeps its place: a HydraDelegationStreamParser field (delegationParser) is fed only each flush's new text for the row, and is reset by endDelegationStream() in startTurn, install, dropDelegationBlock and spawnDelegatedHeads. The parser type itself is specified by PR-HYDRA-095, which does not cite ThreadRuntime. From reading the code: if two assistant rows interleave deltas before any stream exists, the parser is replaced and a resumed row is read only from its new delta. Also, the parser does not require the body to start with '[' or '{' as HydraPrompts.streamedDelegations(inBody:) does. Neither point was run.

The round cap no longer stops later streamed reads of a block that already owns a stream. Tasks that close after the opening read of a request's 3rd round now go out while the reply streams. Before, they were held until spawnDelegatedHeads, whose top-up is still gated on canDelegate.

New public computed property isReadyForHydraMerge. It is true when phase == .idle, the history is not loading, no revert is running, pendingSend == nil, the last turn is .completed, no heads are working, hydraPendingReports, hydraBatches and hydraWaiting are all empty, and no Hydra flush is scheduled. It is used by AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:60, 87, 104, 249 and 681 (outside this batch) to gate merges.
/compact is intercepted locally whenever ProviderKind.supportsCompact is true (Provider.swift:149-154). This adds Claude to the local-compact providers.
The CLI session factory creates ACPSession for the new ProviderKind .opencodeGo.

files.summary: Five changes carry behaviour. (1) The candidate trim at line 61 now uses `.trimmed`, defined at Text.swift:132 as `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)`, so behaviour is identical. (2) The play badge glyph font changed from `.system(size: 13, weight: .semibold)` to `.system(.body, weight: .semibold)` (line 186). (3) AttachmentVideoThumbnail's task now awaits `AttachmentLargePreview.prefetchVideoSize(for:)` before its frame fetch (line 218). (4) videoDisplaySize no longer reads the track synchronously with the deprecated `asset.tracks(withMediaType:)`. A new unbounded @MainActor per-path cache `videoSizes` (line 264) is filled by async `prefetchVideoSize` through `loadTracks`/`load(.naturalSize, .preferredTransform)` (lines 268-279). videoDisplaySize now returns `videoSizes[path] ?? imageBounds` (lines 283-285), so a video whose thumbnail has not appeared or finished prefetching opens at the full 480x360 slot. (5) Caption colours: the large preview footer name went from `.secondary` to `Chrome.secondaryText` and its size text from `.tertiary` to `Chrome.secondaryText` (lines 351, 357). ToolImagePreview's filename went from `.secondary` to `Chrome.secondaryText` (line 425). Everything else is unchanged apart from line shifts.

New app-wide zoom. `AppZoom.levels = [75, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200]`. `normalized` maps any value not in the list to 100. `next` steps to the next higher or lower level and stays put at either end. AppZoomModifier scales content by percent/100 with `scaleEffect(anchor: .topLeading)` inside a private ZoomLayout. ZoomLayout proposes the viewport divided by the scale, so content reflows and keeps its scrollbars inside the window instead of clipping, then reports the child size times the scale and places the child top-leading at the bounds origin. It is applied to every hosted window root and chat column through HostedEnvironment (WindowManager.swift:175). This replaces the conversation-only ChatZoom.

Holds `Font.chat(_ style:, weight:, design:)` with no zoom parameter. It always returns `Font.system(style, design:)` with the resolved weight, and headline defaults to semibold unless another weight is asked for. This is the old ChatZoom.swift zoom == 1 branch (old lines 63-66), kept as the only path. The per-style base-size table and the scaled `Font.system(size:)` branch are gone. The doc comment states that the app-wide zoom scales the window, not the type.

new_behaviours.behaviour: The app zoom levels are exactly [75, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200] percent.
AppZoom.normalized returns the value when it is one of the levels, otherwise 100. It does not clamp to the nearest level.
AppZoom.next normalizes first, then returns the first level above (increasing) or the last level below (decreasing). At either end it returns the current value unchanged.
AppZoomModifier sets scale = normalized(percent)/100 and draws the content with scaleEffect(scale, anchor: .topLeading) inside ZoomLayout.

ZoomLayout proposes the unscaled viewport (proposal width and height divided by the scale) so forms reflow and keep scrollbars inside the window. It reports the child's size times the scale and places the child at bounds.origin, anchored top-leading, with proposal bounds.size/scale. A bigger zoom shows less at once instead of clipping.

Font.chat(style, weight:, design:) is always Font.system(style, design:) with the resolved weight, and headline defaults to semibold. There is no zoom parameter and no point-size scaling; the conversation type no longer scales separately from the app.
New @MainActor static cache `videoSizes: [String: CGSize]` keyed by attachment path. It is unbounded, has no eviction, and lives for the process.

prefetchVideoSize is async. It returns at once unless the attachment isVideo and has no cached size. It loads tracks with `loadTracks(withMediaType: .video)` and the first track's `.naturalSize` and `.preferredTransform`, applies the transform, takes abs values and aspect-fits into 480x360 with floor on each side before caching. On any failure or a zero size it caches nothing, so a later appearance retries.
The video thumbnail's task awaits prefetchVideoSize before its `image == nil` guard and frame grab, so the large preview's panel size depends on the thumbnail having appeared first.
videoDisplaySize now returns videoSizes[path] ?? imageBounds (480x360). A synchronous track read no longer happens on the tap path.

new_behaviours.behaviour: The favicon is fetched from the linked host itself, `https://<host>/favicon.ico`, using a URLRequest with `timeoutInterval = 5`. It is accepted only on a 2xx HTTP status whose body decodes as an NSImage, with no third-party service and no fallback. The 5-second timeout and the single-endpoint rule are not covered by any requirement; PR-THEME-137 still specifies DuckDuckGo then Google.

All markdown type (headings, inline text point size, the mention glyph, the code label and code, the Show buttons) is now independent of any chat zoom. The Copy-message inline link and image rewriting now runs on Swift Regex (`String.replacing` with regex literals), which matches by grapheme cluster instead of NSRegularExpression's UTF-16. The output is the same for ordinary text; it could differ only when a combining mark attaches to a bracket, paren or angle-bracket character. This is from reading the code, not from a test, and no requirement mentions the matching unit.

new_behaviours.behaviour: No MCP argv is passed at all, even when servers are connected. The only scoping is the GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH settings file from ProviderRegistry. The comment gives the reason: an unknown flag makes agy exit 2 with usage text. Side effect: MCPProviderConfig.connectedIDs() (MCPProviderConfig.swift:230) has no caller at 1fbf81e.
Plan-limit reset stamps (bucket.reset_time, and the 4th field of the text fallback) are parsed with ISO8601.date, so stamps with fractional seconds now give a resetsAt.

When a turn result has usage and its spend is above 0, .tokenSpend(TokenSpend) is emitted right after TokenLedger.shared.record(spend: spend.totalTokens). This is a new event for Claude, which emitted none before.

New turnSpendEvent(message, model:). Returns nil with no usage or a zero total. The total is turnSpend. With a non-empty usage.iterations it returns only provider .claude, the total and the model, leaving the parts nil. Otherwise inputTokens = input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens (nil if input_tokens is absent), outputTokens = output_tokens, cachedInputTokens = cache_read_input_tokens, and model = the session's stored model (which can be the configured string, including "default").

Comment only: head task_progress totals are for the head's panel and are deliberately not added to the ledger, to avoid double counting. The code was the same before. This is documentation, not a new code path.

New headModels [String: String] state, filled from thread.model when a head thread starts, on both the parented path and the adopted path. It names the model on a head's .tokenSpend. A head never registered by headStarted (such as a spawn receiver or a subAgentActivity adoption) has no model.

New recordCodexSpend(spend, rolloutID:, model:, agentID:). Nothing happens when spend <= 0. With a non-empty rolloutID it calls TokenLedger.shared.record(codexSpend:rolloutID:), which lowercases the id and adds to liveCodex so the history scan subtracts it. It then always emits .tokenSpend(TokenSpend(provider: .codex, totalTokens: spend, model:, agentID:)). If the lead's threadID is nil or empty, the spend is emitted as an event but NOT written to the ledger; the comment says history owns the daily total in that case.

The lead's spend is attributed to rolloutID threadID and model activeModel. A head's spend is attributed to rolloutID = head id, model = headModels[head] and agentID = head id, and its .tokenSpend comes before the existing .agentProgress.
resetDate's ISO branch now uses ISO8601.date (Date.ISO8601FormatStyle, fractional seconds then plain) instead of ISO8601DateFormatter. Whether edge inputs parse identically is UNKNOWN; not run.
parseDate = ISO8601.date(from:) ?? ISO8601.dateOnly(from:). Quota reset dates with fractional seconds now parse. Before, only whole-second stamps and bare YYYY-MM-DD dates did.
New String.trimmed = trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines). It is behind every cosmetic swap in the 9 files. Recorded so a port does not treat it as a different trim set.

new_behaviours.behaviour: New struct HydraDelegationBudget holding per-request rounds, refusals and dropNotice. canDelegate = rounds < maxDelegationRounds. beginTurn(userAuthored:) resets rounds and refusals only for a user-authored turn (hydraHeads == nil) and never clears dropNotice. chargeRound() adds 1. refuse(_:) returns true and counts the refusal while refusals < maxRefusals (3). Past the cap it calls noteDropped(message) and returns false. noteDropped sets dropNotice = droppedBlockNotice(message), so the last drop wins. takeDropNotice() returns the notice once and clears it. Used at 1fbf81e ThreadRuntime.swift:297, 1208, 1305, 1348, 2783, 2819, 2861, 2868, 2925, 2960, 2965.

Past the refusal cap, a refused block is no longer silent. The refusal text is queued and prepended to the lead's next sent turn as "[Hydra] " + message + "

---

" (ThreadRuntime.swift:1348-1350 at 1fbf81e, taken just before session.send). The unreadable-block message already starts with "[Hydra]", so it reaches the lead as "[Hydra] [Hydra] Your delegation block could not be read...".

New interruptedBlockMessage(stopped:): "No heads went out.\nYour reply's delegation block was dropped: the turn {was stopped|failed} before the heads could go out, and none of that work was delegated. Do it yourself, or send the block again." At 1fbf81e ThreadRuntime.swift:2783 queues it through noteDropped when a turn is interrupted or failed before its block's heads went out. HydraMergeRecord.Outcome adds held and settled (raw "held", "settled"). Doc comment: held means some job files are claimed by another chat's unfinished work, so the merge took nothing and nothing was spent; it goes out once that claim clears. Image downscaling before any provider sees an image (ACPSession, ClaudeSession and OpenAICompatibleSession all call base64Images). maxPixelSize = 2000. If CGImageSource properties report max(pixelWidth, pixelHeight) > 2000, the image becomes a thumbnail (FromImageAlways, WithTransform so EXIF orientation is applied, MaxPixelSize 2000), encoded as public.jpeg at lossy quality 0.8, and the returned attachment copy gets mimeType "image/jpeg". Unreadable-by-ImageIO or small images keep their original bytes and mime. The stored Attachment is not modified. Windows needs an equivalent decoder, orientation-aware resize and JPEG encoder.

new_behaviours.behaviour: openCodeCatalogTask: one shared Task<[ModelOption]?> memoises the opencode ACP catalogue probe per launch for both OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go. The probe always runs ACPSession.probeModels(provider: .opencode, ...). force: true discards the memo before probing, and a nil (thrown) result clears it, but an empty non-nil result stays memoised. Reading the code (not executed): two concurrent forced loads, such as refreshEverything forcing both providers, can each reset the memo and start their own probe.

openCodeModels(_:for:): .opencode keeps ids NOT prefixed "opencode-go/" and .opencodeGo keeps only those, while other providers keep the whole list. Then, for ANY provider, a row name that starts with "<displayName>/" has that prefix removed (e.g. "OpenCode Go/DeepSeek V4 Flash" -> "DeepSeek V4 Flash"). It is applied to cached catalogs at init (172) and to every live catalog before updateCatalog (495).

A delivered OpenCode load fills the sibling: after .opencode or .opencodeGo delivers, the other kind's half of the same raw probe (when non-empty) is written through updateCatalog, gets catalogFetchedAt = now, and is inserted into attemptedCatalogs. storeCatalogDates() is then called again.

model(_:for:) falls back for pre-split threads and pins: when the provider is .opencode, no match is found and the id starts with "opencode-go/", the id is resolved in the .opencodeGo catalogue. Matching was factored into private static match(_:in:), which keeps the exact-then-bracket-prefix logic.
OpenCode Go sessions and probes get MCPSessionOverrides.opencodeEnvironment() merged into their environment, as OpenCode Zen does.
OpenCode Go is re-probed while its catalogue lacks an effort walk (lacksEffortWalk), and its catalogue load goes through openCodeCatalog.

OpenCode Go auth runs the same `opencode auth list` probe. Each U+25CF credential has " api" and " oauth" stripped and empty names dropped. Go reports .signedIn(name) for the first credential containing "opencode go" (localizedCaseInsensitiveContains), otherwise signedOut on exit 0 or unknown on a non-zero exit. Zen reports the first remaining credential, whichever it is.
PlanLimitsReader.read returns nil for .opencodeGo. exposesLimits (68-70) is false for it, so OpenCode Go shows no plan limits.

New ProviderEvent case tokenSpend(TokenSpend), placed after usage(ContextUsage), with a doc comment: it is spend (tokens newly consumed by one request or turn), distinct from usage (context occupancy); a head's spend carries agentID; the turn keeps each report for run metrics. It is consumed at ThreadRuntime.swift:2172 and :2228 (other batch). It makes the pre-existing .tokenSpend emitters compile.

Old: one section per provider in ProviderKind declaration order, each always showing its card. New (SettingsView.swift:584-615): still eager, still one section for every provider, and opening the page still checks nothing. But signed-in providers now come first, then the rest, each group in allCases order (a stable split). Each section is collapsible, with overrides kept in a page-lifetime @State map, providerExpansion. By default a section is expanded only when its provider is signed in.

The card's first row is unchanged: 18pt mark in a 22 frame, 'Checking…'/summary at 13, 'Version <v>' / 'Native API · <host>' at 11, and the enable switch. The section header changed. It is no longer a ChromeSection title but a Button (SettingsView.swift:647-670): ProviderIcon at 16pt, the display name at 13pt semibold .secondary, a Spacer, and a chevron.right at 11pt semibold in Chrome.secondaryText that rotates 90 degrees when expanded. Frame height 22. Tooltip 'Hide the provider settings' / 'Show the provider settings'. Clicking toggles expansion with Chrome.panelSlide. The card shows only when expanded.

Appearance page metadata. Symbol "paintpalette" (drawn by SidebarSymbol at scale 1). Tint Color(red: 0.85, green: 0.44, blue: 0.36). Search keywords: appearance, theme, transparency, transparent, opacity, glass, dark, light, accent, tint, catppuccin, dracula, tokyo, nord, gruvbox, solarized, github, claude, codex, cursor, matrix, text, size, font, zoom, wallpaper, sidebar.
Providers page search keywords gain "opencode zen", "opencode go" and "zen", inserted after "opencode".

The Appearance page renders AppearanceSettingsPage. It is not in pageHasChromeControls, so its content starts 22pt below the sheet edge, and its sticky chrome row shows only the compact title with no accessory.

AppearanceSettingsPage holds one ChromeSection titled "Appearance". Its first card contains, in order: Theme, Transparency, Sidebar, Activity list, and "Open the sidebar at launch" (these rows moved from General unchanged). Then WallpaperCard(). Then AppZoomCard(percent: $settings.appZoom).

AppZoomCard is a ChromeCard with one ChromeRow titled "Zoom". Its detail is "The stock size" at 100%, otherwise "<n>% of the stock size", where n = AppZoom.normalized(appZoom). The trailing HStack(spacing 8) holds, in order: (1) a plain 22x22 button with textformat.size.smaller at .subheadline in Chrome.secondaryText, tooltip "Zoom out", which steps to the previous level and is disabled at the lowest level (75). (2) The text "<n>%" at .subheadline medium with monospaced digits in Chrome.primaryText, minWidth 46. (3) A plain 22x22 button with textformat.size.larger, tooltip "Zoom in", which steps to the next level and is disabled at the highest level (200). (4) A plain 22x22 reset button with arrow.counterclockwise at .subheadline medium, tooltip "Back to the stock size", which sets 100; at 100 it is disabled and has opacity 0 but still takes layout room. The group animates .snappy(duration: 0.2) on the value. No explicit accessibility label or value is set.

AppZoom.levels = [75, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175, 200]. normalized() maps any non-level value to 100. next() steps to the neighbouring level and stays put at either end. AppZoomModifier scales the whole window content: ZoomLayout proposes the unscaled viewport and scaleEffect anchors top-leading, so layout reflows instead of clipping. It is applied at WindowManager.swift:175. The setting AppSettings.appZoom persists under defaults key "appZoom", default 100, normalized on load (AppSettings.swift:131, 253-255, 718). Menu items Zoom In / Zoom Out / Actual Size exist at AppCommands.swift:53-60. Their shortcuts were not examined: UNKNOWN. These belong to other batches' files.

The Providers page orders sections with signed-in providers (auth == .signedIn) first, then all others, each group in ProviderKind.allCases order (a stable split). An auth refresh reorders without animation. Per-provider expansion lives in a page-lifetime @State [ProviderKind: Bool] providerExpansion. With no override, a section is expanded exactly when its provider is signed in, so a provider whose check turns signed-in opens on its own until the user touches its header.

The provider section header is a Button in ChromeQuietButtonStyle (no press feedback; Chrome.swift:276-280), with VStack spacing Chrome.sectionHeaderSpacing. Contents: HStack(spacing 8) of ProviderIcon size 16 in Chrome.primaryText; the display name at .system(size: 13, weight: .semibold) in .secondary; Spacer(minLength: 0); and chevron.right at .system(size: 11, weight: .semibold) in Chrome.secondaryText, rotated 90 degrees when expanded. contentShape rect, frame height 22. Tooltip "Hide the provider settings" when expanded, "Show the provider settings" when collapsed. Accessibility: label = display name, value "Expanded"/"Collapsed", hint "Shows or hides the provider settings", header trait. Click toggles expansion inside withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide).

The provider card sits in ChromeRevealLayout(fraction: isExpanded ? 1 : 0) (Chrome.swift:286-305). The child stays mounted at full size and top-leading, and the slot height is natural height times the fraction, animated. When collapsed the slot is clipped, disabled, not hit-testable and hidden from accessibility. The onAppear/onChange handlers on the section's outer VStack (791-822) still run for collapsed sections: binary path and API key loading, usage refresh, and the 600ms key re-check.

The legend summary text "<n> tokens" carries a tooltip (.help). With no uncertain tokens it reads "Total tokens recorded this year."; otherwise "<m> tokens have an unknown source and may overlap imported history." The same sentence is appended to the accessibility value as "<n> tokens. <detail>" when uncertain tokens exist.

batch:
D04 (DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat + Composer), pinned dd2b86ef (v1.6.0) vs live 1fbf81e (v1.6.2). Read-only; nothing was modified. What I ran: git diff between the two commits for all 9 files (205 insertions and 209 deletions, matching the task list), git grep and git show at both commits, and Python scripts in %TEMP% that pulled every record naming any of the 9 files from porting/spec/*.json and porting/ui_contract.json. That found 412 unique IDs: 275 requirements and 137 UI records. Each UI record in spec/*.json 'ui' is identical to its copy in ui_contract.json (0 differences), so each ID is listed once. A record was flagged for manual review if any cited line fell in a changed hunk on the old side, or if its text named zoom, tertiary, secondary, visibleCount, chronological, compact or trimming. All 140 flagged records were reviewed by hand. The other 272 cite only unchanged code. Results: requirements 246 UNAFFECTED, 27 CHANGED, 1 MOVED, 1 REMOVED; UI records 76 UNAFFECTED, 60 CHANGED, 1 REMOVED.

The changes fall into seven themes:
(1) The chat zoom is gone. Font.chat(style, weight:, design:, zoom:) became Font.chat(style, weight:, design:) (UI/Common/ChatFont.swift:6), and every @Environment(\.chatZoom) was removed. The replacement is the app-wide AppZoom (UI/Common/AppZoom.swift), which uses scaleEffect on the window content; its levels are 75, 90, 100, 110, 125, 150, 175 and 200.
(2) Many views now use Chrome.secondaryText instead of .secondary or .tertiary. Chrome.secondaryText itself changed in Chrome.swift:79, which is outside this batch: it is now 'primaryText.opacity(0.7)' where it was 'Color(nsColor: .secondaryLabelColor)'. Every record that names Chrome.secondaryText therefore renders differently, even where the D04 file did not change. I marked CHANGED only where the record's stated colour now differs.
(3) Fixed sizes were respelled as text styles: 13->.body, 12->.callout, 11->.subheadline, 10->.footnote, 9->.caption2. The pinned ChatZoom.swift chatBaseSize table gives these as the same macOS point sizes, with one exception: caption2 is 10 pt, so the 9 pt xmark in the composer chips grew to 10 pt.
(4) ThreadTimeline's lazy window now anchors on the id of its oldest block (windowStartID) instead of a count (visibleCount).
(5) RowContext.chronological is hardcoded false, so the chronologicalTimeline setting has no reader.
(6) The /compact provider list moved into Provider.supportsCompact.
(7) Some changes are renames with no behaviour change: .trimmed, nonisolated static, and a row() helper extracted.

Spec defect: the MessageEditor citations in PR-CHAT-083..086 and UI-CHAT-015..018 and 065..068 (for example :289, :340-416) point past the end of the pinned file, which has 176 lines. The real code is at :27 and :39-176. No tests or app code were run, so MARROW_PORT_DATA_DIR was not needed.

Old ThreadTimeline.swift:80 '@State private var visibleCount = TimelineWindow.firstPaint' with visible = blocks.suffix(visibleCount), so every appended block pushed the oldest row out. new_behaviours.behaviour: The lazy window is anchored by identity: '@State private var windowStartID: String?' holds the id of the oldest rendered block, and the window runs from that block to the end. A block appended at the end never evicts an older row, so the rendered count grows with the conversation until the thread changes. At pinned, the window was a fixed-size suffix (visibleCount).

Fallback: when windowStartID is nil or its block is no longer in the conversation (for example after a revert removes it), the window shrinks back to the newest TimelineWindow.firstPaint (3) blocks. There was no such fallback at pinned.

loadEarlier(in:to:) takes the blocks. A count keeps the newest count blocks (start = max(0, blocks.count - count)); no count means one page further back (start - 24). The guard 'target < start' means the start only ever moves back, never forward.

The new helper row(_:rewindable:) builds each DisplayBlockView and passes RowContext(chronological: false) at :330. The chronological mode of WorkingIndicator (:2173-2176) and TurnFinishedBlock (TimelineRows.swift:2499-2508) can no longer be reached from the timeline.
The persisted setting key 'chronologicalTimeline' (Bool, default false) is defined at 1fbf81e and read by no view. At dd2b86ef the property had no definition anywhere in the tree.

new_behaviours.behaviour: NEW ChromeQuietButtonStyle. It is a ButtonStyle whose makeBody returns configuration.label unchanged, so a button gives no pressed feedback but keeps Button semantics for keyboard and accessibility. The comment at :275 says so. It is used at 1fbf81e in DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/ModelsSettingsPage.swift:358 and SettingsView.swift:664. It does not exist at dd2b86ef (`git grep` found no match). No requirement covers it.

NEW ChromeRevealLayout, a Layout that reveals its single child by height. `var fraction: CGFloat` is the animatableData. sizeThatFits returns the child's natural width and natural height times the fraction clamped to 0...1, measured with proposal (width, nil). placeSubviews always places the child at bounds.origin, anchored top-leading, at full natural height, so the child stays mounted and does not move while the slot collapses; the doc comment says a clip reveals it in place. It returns .zero when there is no child. It is designed to be driven by a Chrome.panelSlide transaction. It is used at 1fbf81e in ModelsSettingsPage.swift:370, :390 and :394 (fractions `cardVisible ? 1 : 0`, `isVisible && option.id != firstVisibleID ? 1 : 0` and `isVisible ? 1 : 0`) and in SettingsView.swift:671 (`isExpanded ? 1 : 0`). No requirement covers it.

Chrome.secondaryText is now `primaryText.opacity(0.7)`, which is labelColor at 70%. Its stated rationale (:77-78) is that primary at 70% clears the 4.5:1 contrast floor on both backgrounds while secondaryLabelColor's 50% alpha does not. This is an app-wide colour change: 329 uses of Chrome.secondaryText at 1fbf81e. Compound uses such as secondaryText.opacity(0.85), (0.75), (0.8) and (0.6) multiply onto 0.7. Besides the D18-citing records above, a regex scan found up to 345 more requirement and UI record IDs (not checked one by one) that mention a secondary text or label colour and may be stale. Examples: PR-CHAT-074, PR-HYDRA-178, PR-SETTINGS-014, PR-USAGE-012, UI-COMPOSER-005, UI-HYDRA-013, UI-MCP-002 and UI-USAGE-003. The port needs a single token for this, derived from the primary text colour at 0.7 opacity.
ChromeSection headers now use Chrome.secondaryText (labelColor at 0.7) instead of SwiftUI's hierarchical `.secondary` style, so section headings and supporting text now share one secondary colour.

The chrome kit's typography now uses SwiftUI semantic text styles (.body, .callout, .subheadline, .title3) instead of fixed point sizes. Default sizes are unchanged: pinned ChatZoom.swift:44-55 gives body 13, callout 12, subheadline 11, footnote 10, title3 15 and title2 17. Whether these fonts now follow a macOS system text-size setting is UNKNOWN. If they do, the port would need matching text scaling, which no requirement currently covers. Not in this list: ChromeTextMenu, ChromeTextButton and GlassPickerButton titles and the ChromeSearchField text keep their literal 12.5 pt, and chevronFont keeps its literal 8 pt bold.
The same move from literal sizes to text styles (SN) in the other five D18 files. No new strings, settings, controls or branches were added in these five files.
